**(a) Annotation status of HIS-036 and HIS-053**

Neither record carries an annotation. archiefrecords.csv has no remarks column. The kroniek describes the mismatched timestamps only as clerical problems, without naming either record. HIS-112 (dag 15) calls the dag 10 mismatches "Klerkenfouten. Slordigheid, rechtgezet in de marge." HIS-116 (dag 23) attributes the dag 22 mismatch to "een klerk die de nachtdienst niet aankan." Neither is labeled a late entry. Both records are logged before they happened: HIS-036 at dag 9 23:55 for dag 10 04:50, and HIS-053 at dag 22 01:50 for dag 22 04:15. The source does not explain either inversion, so on the archive's own evidence they remain unexplained.

**(b) Other inversions and named dates**

HIS-036 and HIS-053 are the only rows where vastgelegd_op precedes gebeurd_op. I checked every row of the CSV. Two other rows break the equality required by HIS-103 in the opposite direction, logging later than they happened: HIS-035 (gebeurd dag 10 04:45, vastgelegd dag 10 07:20) and HIS-054 (gebeurd dag 22 05:00, vastgelegd dag 22 07:25). The remaining rows are equal or are dated in years before dag 1. HIS-112 names dag 10 and HIS-116 names dag 22 as the days of the mismatched timestamps. Neither names a record ID.

**(c) Corrections or reissues**

The source records no correction or reissue of any Burchtader entry (HIS-035, HIS-049, HIS-054) or any poort oost entry (HIS-053, and the market entries HIS-012, HIS-029, HIS-050, HIS-055, HIS-062, HIS-089). The only correction mentioned is the margin correction referred to in HIS-112. That entry gives no date for the correction and names no record. HIS-116 records a staffing change on dag 23, not a reissue. I have no evidence of any correction on any date.

**Limits**

My earlier reading of HIS-114 as a return of the Stille Winter was unsupported and stays withdrawn. I cannot say whether the rhythm other members describe appears in the archive, because my source contains no wolf, herd, or heavy-night entries.
